artworks.title: Daedalus and Icarus
artworks.description: Van Dyck's wing-fitting: Daedalus prepares the flight that will end in Icarus' fall and the craftsman's later refuge with King Cocalus at Camicus in Sicily.

artworks.title: Daedalus and Icarus
artworks.description: Sacchi's Baroque father and son — the Cretan escape whose survivor Daedalus will shelter under Cocalus' roof when Minos pursues him across the sea.

artworks.title: Minos (detail from The Last Judgment)
artworks.description: Michelangelo's Minos in the Sistine Last Judgment — the judge-king who, in the Sicilian tale, tracks Daedalus to Cocalus and dies in the boiling bath the king's daughters prepare.

popCulture.title: Cocalus
popCulture.description: King of Camicus in Sicily who shelters Daedalus and engineers Minos' death — the western end of the craftsman's exile.

popCulture.title: Daedalus
popCulture.description: Cocalus' famous guest — the labyrinth-builder who flees Crete and finds a second court in Sicily.

popCulture.title: Minos
popCulture.description: The Cretan king who pursues Daedalus with the spiral-shell riddle and dies at Cocalus' palace — hospitality as trap.
